verdicts.reason: A is a narrow vertical stack pushed to x≈228, with ~230px of dead space on the left and an empty strip right of the circle. It reads like the square shrunk onto a banner, though the text column and legal line share a clean left edge. B keeps the original's off-edge circle and spreads the weight across the width, but the legal line is centred under nothing and misaligned with the x≈135 text column, and there is a big empty gap in the middle.

Both use a real banner layout (can, then copy, then CTA in the circle). In both, the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow drops below the body copy, and the legal line is shrunk to illegible ~5px text. B's can is smaller and sits further from the copy, so the left side feels weaker and less balanced than A's bigger, better-anchored can.

A has a sensible left-to-right banner flow, but the eyebrow sits below the body, the legal text is microscopic, and the CTA crowds the right edge. B crams the body copy, 'WEEKEND ONLY' and the wrapped legal text into one tiny line at the bottom, which flattens the hierarchy. It also leaves a dead band under the headline and makes the supporting message barely readable.

A is clean but mostly a vertical stack: big mid-canvas gap, and the legal line is centred out of alignment with the text column. B puts the 'Shop Sale' CTA at the far left before the headline, so the reading order is backwards, and the button nearly touches '20%' (cramped near-collision). Its can is shrunk to a small figure inside the circle, and the legal text is tiny.
